rationale: The candidate reads in all four views as a single object, so it avoids outright fragmentation, but the dominant gesture is weak: a compact stepped/terraced mass rather than one legible long-span gym volume. The silhouette is coherent enough to pass as an early massing study, yet the stepped roof and multiple recesses feel more like stacked platforms than a hall section expressing span or daylight. Most importantly, the verified access edge is answered by a sealed side condition rather than a clear public void, entry seam, or undercut. That makes the ground response semantically opposite to the required threshold logic for a gymnasium. The mass also appears somewhat over-articulated into surface pieces without a strong anchor, reducing hierarchy. The references suggest a simpler, more continuous hall with a pronounced public threshold and/or a carved civic void would be closer to the brief.
